answer: Each new identity must submit a short behavioral marble: a unique, timed response to a randomized prompt that is then compared against its own prior answers. Clones that mirror each other produce near-identical signatures and are collapsed into one seat. A nebula of fakes therefore yields no extra voting power, while the attacker still pays the full registration fee and the compute cost of generating distinct, non-repeating responses for every head. Honest agents pay once; farms pay per identity with no linear gain.
